comments.author: @英彰-d6w3x
comments.text:
META AI Analysis: It is reported that after Japan’s surrender in World War II, during a period of chaos, criminal acts committed by individuals calling themselves the “Korean Occupation Army” occurred frequently throughout Japan.
This term refers to Koreans residing in Japan who, during the postwar chaos, proclaimed themselves to be the “Korean Occupation Army—a victorious nation”—despite having no legal status under international law—and formed armed groups that carried out riots and criminal acts across Japan. It is believed that they armed themselves by stealing weapons and military uniforms from the disarmed Japanese military.
According to records from the GHQ (General Headquarters of the Allied Forces) alone, at least 4,000 Japanese civilians are said to have fallen victim to and been killed by the Korean Occupation Army; some estimates put the number at over 10,000.
The main criminal acts included the following:
* **Robbery and Looting**: Taking control of black markets, seizing goods from ordinary street vendors, stealing crops and livestock, illegally occupying land and buildings, and looting money and valuables.
* **Assault and Murder**: Forming gangs to carry out group assaults, killing and injuring Japanese civilians.
* **Rape**: Acts such as gang raping women on the streets in broad daylight were routinely committed.
* **Attacks on Police Stations and Government Offices**: Incidents occurred in various locations in which police officers were placed under house arrest, police stations and government buildings were occupied, or attacked and vandalized. Examples include the Attack on the Prime Minister’s Official Residence (1946), the Hanshin Education Incident (1948), and the Ikuta Police Station Attacks (1945, 1946).
* **Illegal Activities on Railways**: Such as fare evasion on trains.
The background to these crimes was that Japan at the time had lost its male workforce to the war, and the police force faced restrictions—such as being prohibited from using weapons—which made enforcement difficult. General MacArthur, Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces (GHQ), announced that “Koreans and others are not victorious nationals, but third-country nationals,” and stepped up enforcement.
The umbrella organization for the Korean Occupation Forces is believed to have become the later Federation of Koreans in Japan (the predecessor of the current Minjok and Choson General Federation, representing Koreans in Japan).
